source_documents.title: pH-dependent photoinduced electron transfer of 1,8-naphthalimide derivatives: Effects of regiochemistry, substituent at 4-position and proton receptor

reference_evidence_units.quote: For the probes with piperidine or morpholine as the receptor (compounds 1A-B and 2A-B), PET exhibit pathselective, namely from the distal tertiary amine at 4-substituent to NPA and resulted in fluorescence quench ing.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B
reference_evidence_units.statement: PET only from a receptor on the 4-amino side.

reference_evidence_units.quote: when the solution’s pH changed from 11.0 to 7.01, significant fluorescence enhancement (by 19-fold) was observed accompanied with notable blue-shifts in both absorption (16 nm) and emission (12 nm)
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1B
reference_evidence_units.statement: Protonating the piperidine turns emission on 19-fold.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The protonation of the receptor decreased the fluorescence of 1A/2A, but enhanced that of 1B/2B (Φ> 0.2) significantly, indicating PET is path-dependent for non-acetylated probes 1 and 2.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1A vs 1B

reference_evidence_units.quote: However, the quite small energy gap (0.16 eV, EHOMO -EHOMO-1) makes it difficult for the electron to overcome the reputation barrier, and PET from the proton receptor to the fluorophore is unlikely to happen.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1A
reference_evidence_units.statement: PET from the imide-side receptor is unlikely.

reference_evidence_units.quote: When the receptor is sited at the imide N (1A/2A), PET process is obstructed by the repulsive barrier from the adjacent carbonyl groups to some extent, and therefore 1A/2A emits fluorescence in their neutral states.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1A
reference_evidence_units.statement: Field from the carbonyls blocks PET in 1A.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The slight fluo rescence quenching upon protonation of 1A/2A could possibly be ascribed to the D-PET from the fluorophore to the protonated receptor.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1A (protonated)
reference_evidence_units.statement: 15% quenching on protonation, tentatively reverse PET.

reference_evidence_units.quote: For probe 1B, electron density in the LUMO is situated on the fluorophore, that in the HOMO is distributed over the fluorophore and the piperidine ring, and the HOMO-1 electron density is primarily localized on the proton receptor (Fig. 6), theoretically sup porting the proposed PET process (Fig. 4).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1B

reference_evidence_units.quote: It is interesting to note that the decrease in pH initiated prominent fluores cence enhancements for both 1A-Ace and 1B-Ace (Fig. 3a-b), implying that PET process is activated upon acetylation of the 4-amino.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1A-Ace
reference_evidence_units.statement: After acetylation even the imide-side receptor quenches; protonation gives 12-fold enhancement (Table 1).

reference_evidence_units.quote: For 1A-Ace, the much higher energy gap between HOMO and HOMO-1 (0.79 eV) along with the attractive field at 4-position makes the PET process easier [55].
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1A-Ace
reference_evidence_units.statement: Acetylation lowers the fluorophore orbital and enables PET.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Taking probe 1A as an example, Fig. 5 demonstrates that 1A exhibits significant charge separation capability: the molecule exhibits ground-state polarization or donor-acceptor character.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1A
reference_evidence_units.statement: 4-amino donor and imide acceptor give push-pull character.

reference_evidence_units.quote: The higher Sr index (0.72178 a.u. for 1A vs 0.80511 a.u. for 1A-Ace) induced by acetylation confirms greater overlap be tween the hole and electron distributions, demonstrating that the ICT process is attenuated upon acetylation.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1A vs 1A-Ace
reference_evidence_units.statement: 1A has a CT-type S1; acetylation reduces it.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Compared to their parent compounds, acetylation led to 80–100 nm blue shifts in both absorption and emission maxima.
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1A vs 1A-Ace
reference_evidence_units.statement: Weaker ICT after acetylation shifts spectra to the blue.

reference_evidence_units.quote: Acetylation led to similar changes in Sr, D index and t index values of 1B (Fig. S5).
reference_evidence_units.subject: 1B
reference_evidence_units.statement: 1B has the same CT-type S1 as 1A.

reference_mechanisms.label: ICT_TICT_CT
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Same CT-type S1 as 1A by hole-electron analysis.

reference_mechanisms.label: PET_ET
reference_mechanisms.rationale: Neutral 1B is dark (Φ < 0.03) and protonation of the piperidine turns emission on 19-fold; orbital localisation supports PET from the 4-side receptor.

contrast_group.varied_factor: relative to 1A: receptor moved from the imide N to the 4-amino side (1B), or 4-amino acetylated (1A-Ace)
contrast_group.paper_difference: 1A: no PET, bright in neutral form; 1B: PET from the 4-side receptor, dark until protonated; 1A-Ace: acetylation activates PET from the imide-side receptor.
